# Superseded ADR — the supersedes link in the link graph's spelling

# `superseded_requires_link` holds only when the body links the target
# `supersedes` names. The fixture declares `supersedes: decisions/old-adr` and
# its body links [[Old Pipeline]](decisions/old-adr.md): the .md-bearing
# destination and the .md-less field name are the same target only if CEL
# normalizes the explicit destination to the spelling the link graph records,
# so the write itself is the normalization check and `akb links` shows that one
# spelling resolving to the page. The same page with a body link to a different
# destination is refused, and the report names no other adr rule — the failing
# rule is the link check alone.

# --- Setup ---

# Every invocation names its base explicitly: the harness default (AKB_KB=.)
# resolves against the working directory of each command, so the scenario pins
# the absolute path it created instead — the same base however the commands are
# scheduled, and whatever else shares TMPDIR.
env AKB_KB=
exec akb init sa-kb
env AKB_KB=$WORK/sa-kb
cd sa-kb

# init seeds no templates: copy the adr template for the pages this scenario
# writes.
exec akb template get adr --full --examples
cp stdout .agent-kb/templates/adr.yaml
exec git add .agent-kb/templates
exec git commit -m 'seed adr template'

# The record the superseded page names.
stdin ../old-adr.md
exec akb write decisions/old-adr.md
stdout 'Written to kb/decisions/old-adr.md'

# --- PASS: superseded, supersedes set, body link matches in another spelling ---

stdin ../superseded-adr.md
exec akb write decisions/superseded-adr.md
stdout 'Written to kb/decisions/superseded-adr.md'

exec akb links decisions/superseded-adr.md
stdout 'Outbound:'
stdout '  decisions/old-adr -> kb/decisions/old-adr.md'

# --- FAIL: the same page with a link to a destination supersedes never names ---

stdin ../wrong-link-adr.md
! exec akb write decisions/wrong-link-adr.md
stderr 'superseded_requires_link'
stderr 'superseded ADRs must link the ADR named by supersedes'
# Every other adr validation rule holds for this page, so the report carries
# superseded_requires_link and no other rule id.
! stderr 'require_title'
! stderr 'title_no_period'
! stderr 'title_style'
! stderr 'valid_status'
! stderr 'tags_nonempty'
! stderr 'tags_format'
! stderr 'require_context'
! stderr 'require_decision'
! stderr 'require_consequences'
! stderr 'disallow_options'
! stderr 'disallow_pros_cons'
! stderr 'min_word_count'
! stderr 'code_blocks_have_language'
! stderr 'valid_state_transition'
! stderr 'created_immutable'
! stderr 'updated_not_before_created'
! stderr 'temporal_created'
! stderr 'superseded_requires_field'
! stderr 'proposed_has_no_supersedes'
! stderr 'require_wikilink'
! exists kb/decisions/wrong-link-adr.md

-- old-adr.md --
---
type: adr
title: Adopt the Original Pipeline
summary: The first pipeline this record set adopts
tags: [pipeline]
status: accepted
deciders: akb maintainers
created: '2026-01-05'
updated: '2026-02-10'
---

# Adopt the Original Pipeline

This record adopts the first version of the ingestion pipeline, the one the
superseding decision replaces. It is kept in the set as the predecessor every
later pipeline record links back to, so the chain of decisions stays readable
without opening the git history of a retired design.

## Context

The knowledge base needed a single way to turn raw sources into indexed pages.
Every alternative at the time either hid the transform behind a service the
maintainers could not inspect or wrote pages that failed validation after the
fact, so the team settled on a small in-process pipeline whose steps are
visible in the repository. The record below captures that first shape and the
constraints that made it the right move at the time.

## Decision

Adopt the in-process pipeline: read a source, transform it, validate the
result, and write one page. See [[decisions/superseded-adr]] for the record
that replaces this one.

## Consequences

The pipeline is inspectable and its failures are local to one run. It also
runs in the CLI process, so long sources block the command that ingests them,
which is the limitation the successor record addresses.

-- superseded-adr.md --
---
type: adr
title: Supersede the Original Pipeline
summary: The pipeline this set adopts in place of the original
tags: [pipeline]
status: superseded
deciders: akb maintainers
created: '2026-02-11'
updated: '2026-03-01'
supersedes: decisions/old-adr
---

# Supersede the Original Pipeline

This record supersedes [[Old Pipeline]](decisions/old-adr.md) and carries the
pipeline shape the set now follows, while the older record stays in place as
the predecessor it replaced. The body link spells its destination with a .md
suffix while the supersedes field does not, so the write proves the two
spellings resolve to one target.

## Context

The original pipeline blocked the CLI on long sources, and the workaround of
splitting a source by hand moved the failure outside the tool. The team needed
an ingest step that yields between chunks, so a long run stays cancellable and
a partial run leaves the index consistent with the pages on disk.

## Decision

Read, transform, validate, and write one chunk at a time, and record the
position of the last completed chunk in the pipeline state. The superseded
record remains reachable from this page, so a reader can follow the chain of
decisions from the original design to this replacement.

## Consequences

Runs stay cancellable and resumable. The trade is a state file that must be
committed with the pages it describes, and a reader who wants the full history
must follow the link to the superseded record.

updated: '2026-03-01'
supersedes: decisions/old-adr
---

# Wrong Link Pipeline Record

This record claims to supersede the original pipeline but links
[[Old Pipeline]](decisions/renamed-adr.md) instead, a destination the
supersedes field never names. Every other rule holds, so the write fails on the
supersedes link alone and the report names that rule and no other.

## Context

The original pipeline blocked the CLI on long sources, and the workaround of
splitting a source by hand moved the failure outside the tool. The team needed
an ingest step that yields between chunks, so a long run stays cancellable and
a partial run leaves the index consistent with the pages on disk.

## Decision

Read, transform, validate, and write one chunk at a time, and record the
position of the last completed chunk in the pipeline state. The superseded
record remains reachable from this page, so a reader can follow the chain of
decisions from the original design to this replacement.

## Consequences

Runs stay cancellable and resumable. The trade is a state file that must be
committed with the pages it describes, and a reader who wants the full history
must follow the link to the superseded record.
